newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian shares take breather from bull run.
newsitem.headline: Italian shares take breather from bull run.

text.p: The Italian stock market finally took a break from its recent bull run after setting fresh index peaks on Tuesday and ended unchanged after choppy trading.
The blue-chip Mib30 and the all-share Mibtel indices both tore to fresh peaks at 20,570 and 13,499 respectively before profit-taking set in to knock them back.
The Mib30 index closed 0.06 percent up at 20,249 while the Mibtel ended 0.01 percent lower at 13,316.
Analysts noted however both indices are only three to four years old and the market is in fact not yet at its all-time high of 1986 when the widely watched BCI index peaked at 908.20.
The BCI index, which is updated only once a day, stood 1.42 percent higher at 839.27.

The market saw volatile trade with slippage at the start from Monday's weaker Wall Street before the stocks recovered on a wave of buying in state-controlled energy group ENI and state telecoms holding Stet.
Sales, possibly from abroad, then set in at the peaks, brokers said.
ENI closed up 1.19 percent at 9,503 as a public share offer for a third tranche of its stock continued with plenty of interest.
Among other industrials, dairy products group Parmalat Finanziaria fell 2.02 percent to 2519.

The company met analysts late on Monday but failed to impress, with analysts saying they were concerned about prospects for falling global margins and some uncertainty over the validity of strategy in mature north American markets.
